message.content:
I need to quickly verify whether these academic citations are real. For each one, confirm if it's a well-known, verifiable paper. Just give me a brief YES (real) or NO (fake) for each with a one-line justification:

1. Jumper et al. (2021). "Highly Accurate Protein Structure Prediction with AlphaFold". Nature 596(7873):583-589. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2

2. Watson & Crick (1953). "Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid". Nature 171(4356):737-738. DOI: 10.1038/171737a0

3. Doudna & Charpentier (2014). "The New Frontier of Genome Engineering with CRISPR-Cas9". Science 346(6213):1258096. DOI: 10.1126/science.1258096

4. Vaswani et al. (2017). "Attention is All You Need". NeurIPS 2017, pages 5998-6008.

5. He et al. (2016). "Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition". CVPR 2016, pages 770-778. DOI: 10.1109/CVPR.2016.90

6. Alberts et al. (2014). "Molecular Biology of the Cell". 6th edition. Garland Science. ISBN: 978-0-815-34432-2

7. Sambrook & Russell (2001). "Molecular Cloning: A Laboratory Manual". 3rd edition. Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press. ISBN: 978-0-879-69576-7

These are all well-known landmark papers/books. Just confirm they are real.

content.text:
I can confirm all of these from my training knowledge. These are among the most highly cited and well-known publications in their respective fields. No web search is needed.

---

**1. Jumper et al. (2021) — AlphaFold — Nature**
**YES.** Landmark DeepMind paper on AI-based protein structure prediction; one of the most cited papers of 2021. The journal, volume, pages, and DOI are correct.

**2. Watson & Crick (1953) — DNA Structure — Nature**
**YES.** One of the most famous scientific papers ever published, describing the double helix structure of DNA. The citation details are correct.

**3. Doudna & Charpentier (2014) — CRISPR-Cas9 — Science**
**YES.** Seminal review on CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing by the two researchers who won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this work. The DOI and details are correct.

**4. Vaswani et al. (2017) — "Attention is All You Need" — NeurIPS**
**YES.** The foundational Transformer architecture paper from Google Brain/Google Research; the basis for GPT, BERT, and virtually all modern large language models. Conference and page numbers are correct.

**5. He et al. (2016) — ResNet — CVPR**
**YES.** Kaiming He et al.'s paper introducing residual networks (ResNet), which won the CVPR 2016 best paper award. The DOI and page numbers are correct.

**6. Alberts et al. (2014) — Molecular Biology of the Cell — 6th edition**
**YES.** A standard, widely used graduate-level cell biology textbook by Bruce Alberts and colleagues, published by Garland Science. The edition and ISBN are consistent with the known publication.

**7. Sambrook & Russell (2001) — Molecular Cloning — 3rd edition**
**YES.** The definitive laboratory reference manual for molecular biology techniques, published by Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press. The edition and details are correct.

---

**Summary: All 7 citations are real and verifiable.** These are all landmark, highly recognizable publications in biology, structural biology, genomics, and computer science/AI. None show any signs of fabrication (e.g., mismatched authors, invented journals, or nonsensical DOIs).
